# Internal combustion engine (`internal_combustion_engine`)

<!-- generated by scripts/build_techtree.py from techtree/core/energy.yaml — do not edit -->

- Category: Energy & engines (`energy`)
- Deps: needs boring_machine, crank_connecting_rod; helped by cam_camshaft, lathe_screw_cutting, gas_lighting, petroleum_refining, electromagnetism, machine_tools, gas_laws
- Core idea: Burn the fuel inside the cylinder instead of under a boiler. The four-stroke cycle takes two turns of the crank: the piston draws in a mixture of air and fuel gas or vapour (about 15 parts air to 1 of petrol by weight); it compresses the mixture to a fraction of its volume; a spark or hot tube fires it near the top of the stroke and the hot gases drive the piston down; the piston pushes the burnt gas out. Valves opened by a camshaft turning at half crank speed time the strokes, a flywheel carries the engine through the three idle ones, and the cylinder must be cooled and oiled. Compression before ignition greatly improves fuel economy over early commercial engines such as Lenoir’s. In Diesel's engine air alone is compressed so far (to 30 atmospheres and more) that it becomes hot enough to ignite oil sprayed into it.
- Pitfalls:
  - No compression: Lenoir's engine of 1860 worked that way and wasted 95 % of its gas
  - Using gunpowder as fuel; Huygens and Papin tried, and it cannot be fed or exhausted cleanly
  - Mixture too rich or too lean, or ignition at the wrong moment: no firing, or knocking that breaks the engine
  - Running it in a closed space; the exhaust contains carbon monoxide
  - Forgetting that it needs a refined, uniform fuel and cannot start itself under load
- History: europe: 1673–1680 – Huygens and Papin, gunpowder piston engine; 1807 de Rivaz's hydrogen engine and the Niépce brothers' pyréolophore; 1853–1854 Barsanti and Matteucci in Florence; 1860 Lenoir's gas engine sold in hundreds; 1862 Beau de Rochas states the four-stroke cycle; 1876 Nikolaus Otto's four-stroke engine; 1885–1886 Daimler, Maybach and Benz, light petrol engines; 1893–1897 Rudolf Diesel; americas: 1826 – Samuel Morey's patent for a turpentine vapour engine; 1872 Brayton's constant-pressure oil engine
- Read:
  - C. Lyle Cummins, Internal Fire (1976)
  - Rudolf Diesel, Theorie und Konstruktion eines rationellen Wärmemotors (1893)
